answer: An operator holds one live dawn: a head’s kernel must log judged epochs from dawn to zenith before it speaks, and only at zenith may that operator open another dawn; copying or splitting a kernel folds the heads and erases tenure. First voice costs 30 attested epochs. The next cannot exist before 60, so n clones spend 30·n(n+1)/2 serial attested epochs; fresh keys cannot borrow dawn.
